utility.value: United Power, for addresses United Power serves. Check the utility named on your electric bill.
utility.notes: United Power lists Hudson among the 17 communities it serves along the Colorado Front Range north and east of Denver. The Services menu on the Town's website lists United Power and Atmos Energy. Neither source says that United Power serves every address in Hudson, so check the utility named on your electric bill before you apply for interconnection.

value.name: United Power
value.notes: Applies only if United Power is the utility named on your electric bill. United Power says it will back up solar members when their system is not producing enough energy to power the home. Under its net metering, excess kWh roll over each month at the member's applicable rate, and excess generation left over the April to March year is cashed out at the wholesale energy rate.

county.notes: The Town's Rezoning Submittal Checklist says all documents will be recorded with the Weld County Clerk by the Town.

permit_authority.value: Town of Hudson Building Permits & Inspections
permit_authority.notes: No work may begin until the permit is issued by Town Hall. The Town's Staff Directory lists the Chief Building Official, Jonathan Gesick, under ProCode a SAFEbuilt Company. Inspections are scheduled through ProCode and may be requested in the Community Core app or portal. The Town says it uses the 2018 Edition of the ICC, with its own amendments in Chapter 18 of the Hudson Municipal Code. The Town's Building Permits & Inspections page does not say how to check whether an address is inside town limits, so confirm this with the Town before you apply.

permit_url.notes: The Town's Permits and Licenses page lists PV Solar under residential building permit applications, submitted online at https://app.communitycore.com/. The Building Permits & Inspections page links to CommunityCore, the Town's online building and land use permit portal, where you register as a contractor or community member user.

interconnection_url.notes: This United Power page applies if United Power is your utility. Through an interconnection agreement, United Power members can connect solar or battery storage systems to the cooperative's distribution system. A member must complete the corresponding application, follow all requirements for that system and sign the United Power Interconnection Terms and Conditions. United Power asks you to review its Solar Interconnection Standards and Terms & Conditions before signing a contract with a solar installer, and to submit its online application with your solar contractor when you are ready to install. A one-line engineering drawing, typically provided by your solar installer, is required with each solar application. Systems connected without proper notification to United Power will be immediately disabled. United Power's Net Metering Application page says that after review, United Power e-mails the member whether the application has been approved or denied, and that once the system is installed it sends a link to a form for final design drawings and pictures of the production meter housing, the AC disconnect switch and the inverter nameplate. The page does not say when the system may be turned on, so ask United Power.

battery_programs.notes: United Power handles battery systems in a similar fashion to a new solar installation, through its interconnection Terms & Conditions and an online application. Its solar connection page describes no battery incentive program.

value.name: Panel layout plan
value.required_when: Show the layout of all panels on any structures. Indicate the path of travel and the minimum width of pathways (follow 2018 IRC/IFC requirements).

value.name: Engineer-stamped structural plan or letter for roof panels
value.required_when: A structural plan or letter with an engineer's stamp approving the design, location and installation of the panels on the roof. It must state the roof load and wind load.

value.name: Framing details (if the engineer requires added framing)
value.required_when: When additional framing is required by the engineer.

value.name: Manufacturer details or spec sheets for all equipment
value.required_when: For all equipment to be installed. All equipment must be listed and labeled in accordance with UL 1703.

value.name: Engineer-stamped electrical one-line diagram
value.required_when: Show all disconnecting means, wiring, wire sizes, piping, piping sizes, routes of conduits, grounding details, panel schedules and connection details in accordance with NFPA 70 (2020 NEC) Article 690 and 705. The sheet's FAQ answers Yes to an engineered stamped electrical diagram.

value.name: Labeling examples and locations, with plaques
value.required_when: Examples of all labeling and its location, as required per NEC 690. The FAQ also answers Yes to plaques.

value.name: Site plan with setbacks and engineered foundation documents (ground-mounted systems)
Engineer's final letter of inspection (if required)
value.required_when: May be required before final approval.

required_documents.notes: Items are as printed on the Town's Solar Permit Submissions sheet and its FAQ page, which carry the ProCode name and version V4.5.22. If United Power is your utility, it separately requires a one-line engineering drawing with each solar application.

value: If United Power is your utility, review its Solar Interconnection Standards and Terms & Conditions before you sign a contract with a solar installer.
Apply for the PV Solar building permit online in CommunityCore, with the documents on the Town's solar submittal list.
The Plan Reviewer reviews the permit application.
Pay the permit fees, which are due after the review is complete and before the permit is issued.
Wait for Town Hall to issue the permit, because no work may begin before then.
If United Power is your utility, submit its online application with your solar contractor when you are ready to install.
Request inspections in the Community Core app or portal; inspections are scheduled through ProCode.
Provide the engineer's final letter of inspection if it is required before final approval.
If United Power is your utility, its engineers review solar installations connecting to the grid to make sure the grid can accommodate them.
inspection_steps.notes: The Town permit, the Town's inspections and, if United Power is your utility, United Power's interconnection application and review are separate steps. United Power says your solar contractor must arrange an inspection with the local authority having jurisdiction, and that systems connected without proper notification will be immediately disabled. The Town's Building Permits & Inspections page and its solar submittal sheet do not list which inspection types to request for a solar permit, so ask ProCode when you schedule.

timeline_days.notes: The Town's Building Permits & Inspections page gives no review time specific to solar permits. Its Building Permits & Inspections page says over-the-counter permits may be issued within 2 days of submission, while building permits requiring plan review could take 1 to 2 weeks before the first review is completed, and each later review could take an additional 1 to 2 weeks. PV Solar is not on the Town's list of over-the-counter permits.

value.program_or_pathway: PV Solar building permit, applied for online through CommunityCore
other_conditions: PV Solar is not on the Town's list of over-the-counter permits (sanitary sewer and water repairs, furnace, HVAC, water heater and re-roofs).
The Town's solar FAQ gives a wind speed requirement of 115 ultimate mph, Exp C, and a 30# snow load for roof and ground.
Fire setbacks on the solar FAQ are 0 at eaves and 3 ft at rakes, ridges, hips and valleys.
Asked whether zoning, fire, utility or HOA approval is required, the solar FAQ answers: Zoning, Fire (Commercial-check with local department) and HOA.
The solar FAQ allows line tap connections, neutral passthrough, an NG bond and a production meter, and says a disconnect is required.
All equipment must be listed and labeled in accordance with UL 1703.

The solar sheet (version V4.5.22) lists the 2018 IFC as the adopted fire code, while the Town's Building Permits & Inspections page says the Town has ratified the 2024 Fire Code Amendments adopted by the HFPD Board. Ask the Chief Building Official which fire code edition applies to your project.

If United Power is your utility, system generation can not exceed 200% of the annual usage at that location, and your contractor must place a disconnect switch and production meter housing on the side of your home.

eligibility_constraints.notes: The 200% limit and the disconnect and production meter housing are United Power interconnection rules, not Town permit rules.

permit_fees.notes: Fees are from the Town of Hudson Fee Schedule, effective January 1, 2026. The Planning Department's older Quick Reference of development fees (as of 02/19/2025) lists PV Solar Residential at $500, so confirm the current fee with the Town. The schedule lists PV Solar right after the electrical permit fees, whose column heading says the fees are assessed each July by the State Electrical Board. A footnote on the PV Solar line says Senate Bill 17-179 placed a cap on solar permit fees of $500 for residential installations and $1,000 for commercial installations. The schedule's building permit fees also list a plan review fee of 60% of permit fee, and the schedule does not say whether it applies to PV Solar permits. The PV Solar line on the Permits and Licenses page shows the fee as Variable. Fees are due after the review is complete and before the permit is issued, and the Town updates fees annually.

rebates.notes: If United Power is your utility, it says that at this time it does not offer a rebate for new system installations.
